sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.

sentences.en: Some years ago, I got to talking with an investor.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我和一位投资者聊过天。

sentences.en: By his own account, he was a one-percenter.

sentences.en: Like many other successful Americans before him,
sentences.zh: 像许多在他之前的成功美国人一样，

sentences.zh: 他在成长过程中克服了许多挑战。

sentences.en: And then he told me about the one thing in his life that made him sad.
sentences.zh: 然后他告诉我，他生命中有一件事让他感到难过。

sentences.en: His kids.
sentences.zh: 他的孩子们。

sentences.en: They were sweet and smart, but they lacked drive.
sentences.zh: 他们很可爱也很聪明，但缺乏动力。

sentences.en: They had led easy lives, he told me.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，他们过着优越的生活。

sentences.en: I've heard variations of the same story over the years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，我听过各种类似的故事。

sentences.en: People who have come through adversity will invariably tell you
sentences.zh: 经历过逆境的人总是会告诉你，

sentences.en: that their adversity played a central role in their success.
sentences.zh: 逆境在他们的成功中发挥了核心作用。

sentences.en: This idea that hard times make us stronger has been touted so often
sentences.zh: 这种“苦难使我们更强大”的观点被如此频繁地宣扬，

sentences.en: and by so many people that we rarely stop to ask ourselves,
sentences.zh: 被如此多的人提及，以至于我们很少停下来问自己：

sentences.en: is there any truth to the story?
sentences.zh: 这个说法有道理吗？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we explore whether adversity
sentences.zh: 本周在《隐藏的大脑》中，我们将探讨逆境

sentences.en: is the secret sauce of success.
sentences.zh: 是否是成功的秘诀。

sentences.en: Iranda Jayavikrama grew up in Sri Lanka while a civil war raged in that country.
sentences.zh: 伊兰达·贾亚维克拉马在斯里兰卡长大，当时该国正处于内战之中。

sentences.en: When he was 21, he moved to the United States to study.
sentences.zh: 21岁时，他移居美国求学。

sentences.zh: 抵达后不久，伊兰达开始注意到美国人

sentences.zh: 对逆境和苦难的看法与他所熟知的截然不同。

sentences.en: It became the start of a lifelong exploration.
sentences.zh: 这开启了他终身的探索。

sentences.en: Today, as a psychologist at Wake Forest University, Iranda is asking a question
sentences.zh: 如今，作为维克森林大学的心理学家，伊兰达正在探究一个

sentences.en: that is increasingly relevant in many parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 在世界许多地方都日益重要的问题。

sentences.zh: 人们在经历可怕的时刻时会发生什么，

sentences.en: Iranda Jayavikrama, welcome to Hidden Brain.

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.

sentences.zh: 所以到那时，你开始在宾夕法尼亚大学成为一名心理学家。

sentences.en: but they have to deal now with the expectations that, you know, they've been bequeathed a gift to actually become some kind of superior person,
sentences.zh: 你当时正在读研究生。

sentences.en: you know, some kind of superhero.
sentences.zh: 你发现“战胜逆境”的套路，或者说“超级英雄”的套路，不仅在美国流行文化中占据主导地位，

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 而且它还渗透到了我们对心理健康和人类潜能的理解中。

sentences.en: And I think it's especially strange to be given that type of advice, right, that this is a gift, this is opportunity.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是一种文化叙事，它还开始影响科学研究。

sentences.en: When you are still sort of thinking about the emotional response that you have when you're given the news, right,
sentences.zh: 心理学家开始研究“创伤后成长”这一概念。

sentences.en: that it seems very quick to move from, oh, you have this like very serious situation to, oh, but this is an opportunity that you can learn from.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很科学，对吧？

sentences.en: Or this is an opportunity where you can sort of grow your character, become the best possible version of yourself.
sentences.zh: 但伊兰达怀疑，这实际上只是我们文化中那种“杀不死你的只会让你更强大”的叙事在科学界的翻版。

sentences.en: So by this point, you were starting to become a psychologist at the University of Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅希望人们在经历创伤后恢复正常，

sentences.en: You were in grad school.
sentences.zh: 我们还希望他们变得比以前更好。

sentences.en: And you discovered that the triumphing over adversity trope or, you know, the superhero trope was not only dominant in American popular culture,
sentences.zh: 这给那些正在遭受苦难的人带来了巨大的压力。

sentences.en: but it was a booming area in psychological research.
sentences.zh: 但当时这在心理学研究领域是一个蓬勃发展的方向。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about the idea of post-traumatic growth?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我讲讲“创伤后成长”这个概念吗？

sentences.en: What does that mean and how that connected with this larger cultural trope?
sentences.zh: 它是什么意思？它又是如何与这种更宏大的文化隐喻联系在一起的？

sentences.en: Post-traumatic growth refers to this idea that people can experience positive psychological changes as a result of going through stressful life experiences.
sentences.zh: “创伤后成长”指的是这样一种观点：人们在经历压力重重的生活事件后，可能会产生积极的心理变化。

sentences.en: Research on post-traumatic growth, you know, sort of started taking off in the mid-1990s.
sentences.zh: 关于创伤后成长的研究，你知道，大约是在 20 世纪 90 年代中期开始兴起的。

sentences.en: A lot of the early research on post-traumatic growth, I think, was based on interviews that clinicians were doing with clients who had gone through trauma, gone through adversity.
sentences.zh: 我认为，早期关于创伤后成长的大量研究，是基于临床医生对那些经历过创伤、经历过逆境的客户所做的访谈。

sentences.en: And they were trying to categorize the types of benefits these clients would report in their clinical interviews.
sentences.zh: 他们试图将这些客户在临床访谈中报告的益处进行分类。

sentences.en: And in the last 20 years, you know, work and research and interest in post-traumatic growth has exploded.
sentences.zh: 而在过去 20 年里，你知道，人们对创伤后成长的投入、研究和兴趣呈爆炸式增长。

sentences.en: I can tell you that in the last six months, I think I've seen at least three papers looking at post-traumatic growth in the wake of COVID.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你，在过去六个月里，我想我至少看到了三篇研究新冠疫情后创伤后成长的论文。

sentences.en: And I'm sure there are quite a few more that are in the pipeline.
sentences.zh: 而且我敢肯定，还有不少论文正在筹备中。

sentences.en: Even as some clinicians were telling patients that traumatic events could lead to growth, other researchers said, hang on.
sentences.zh: 即使一些临床医生告诉病人创伤事件可能带来成长，其他研究人员却说，等等。

sentences.en: Are people reporting growth because they've grown?
sentences.zh: 人们报告成长是因为他们真的成长了吗？

sentences.en: Or are they saying so because the superhero trope is so dominant in the culture?
sentences.zh: 还是因为“超级英雄”的隐喻在文化中占据主导地位，所以他们才这么说？

sentences.en: Iranda cites a paper by the researcher Patricia Frazier.
sentences.zh: 伊兰达引用了研究员帕特里夏·弗雷泽的一篇论文。

sentences.en: So, I was a graduate student when I started becoming interested in looking at post-traumatic growth.
sentences.zh: 我当时还是一名研究生，刚开始对研究创伤后成长产生兴趣。

sentences.en: And I remember reading this paper when it came out.
sentences.zh: 我记得这篇论文发表时我读过它。

sentences.en: And it was a very, you know, elegant, simple paper.
sentences.zh: 那是一篇非常，你知道，优雅且简洁的论文。

sentences.en: It was a short-term, longitudinal study.
sentences.zh: 那是一项短期的纵向研究。

sentences.en: So, it was a study that tracked a large number of undergraduate students over a few months.
sentences.zh: 这项研究在几个月内追踪了大量的本科生。

sentences.en: And it asked them whether they experienced a major stressful event.
sentences.zh: 它询问他们是否经历过重大的压力事件。

sentences.en: And then they were asked, okay, as a result of the stressful event, how much have you changed because of the trauma?
sentences.zh: 然后问他们，好吧，由于这次压力事件，因为创伤，你改变了多少？

sentences.en: And so, it turns out that this question, how much do you think you've changed because of the trauma, is the way most measures of post-traumatic growth asks about change.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，这个问题——“你认为因为创伤你改变了多少”——正是大多数衡量创伤后成长的方法询问变化的方式。

sentences.en: And this paper made me realize that even though most theories about post-traumatic growth were talking about post-traumatic growth in terms of personality transformation,
sentences.zh: 这篇论文让我意识到，尽管大多数关于创伤后成长的理论都是从人格转化的角度来谈论创伤后成长的，

sentences.en: the measures of post-traumatic growth were actually looking at something different, which was the perception of change.
sentences.zh: 但衡量创伤后成长的指标实际上是在观察不同的东西，即对变化的感知。

sentences.en: And what they found was that while people who had experienced real change had better quality mental health,
sentences.zh: 他们发现，虽然那些真正经历过改变的人心理健康状况更好，

sentences.en: the people who reported perceiving high levels of change as a result of experiencing the trauma or the adverse event actually reported higher levels of mental distress.
sentences.zh: 但那些报告称因经历创伤或逆境而感知到高度变化的人，实际上报告了更高水平的心理困扰。

sentences.en: So, from the point of view of someone who was now just looking at this larger, you know, American cultural trope,
sentences.zh: 所以，从一个现在正审视这种更宏大的、你知道，美国文化隐喻的人的角度来看，

sentences.en: what I'm going to now call the superhero trope, that, you know, bad things produce extraordinary qualities to come out inside you,
sentences.zh: 我现在称之为“超级英雄隐喻”，即，你知道，坏事会激发你内在非凡的品质，

sentences.en: is it fair to say that this study in some ways was pointing to the fact that if you subscribe very strongly to this belief,
sentences.zh: 那么，如果说这项研究在某种程度上指出了这样一个事实：如果你非常强烈地认同这种信念，

sentences.en: this superhero trope belief, but didn't actually have the changes in your life,
sentences.zh: 这种超级英雄隐喻的信念，但实际上你的生活中并没有发生这些改变，

sentences.en: not only was this not good, but it could actually be bad.
sentences.zh: 这不仅不好，甚至可能是有害的，这种说法公平吗？

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为是对的。

sentences.en: What was happening was that people were having these beliefs about benefits or growth that experience
sentences.zh: 发生的情况是，人们持有这些关于益处或成长的信念，

sentences.en: as a way to cope with the traumatic event that had gone through.
sentences.zh: 以此作为应对他们所经历的创伤事件的一种方式。

sentences.en: So, in some ways, having these beliefs was potentially serving the role of making them think about the event in a more manageable way,
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种程度上，持有这些信念可能起到了让他们以更易于掌控的方式思考事件的作用，

sentences.en: maybe make them establish a greater sense of control over the event.
sentences.zh: 也许能让他们对事件建立起更强的掌控感。

sentences.en: And I think one lesson from the Frasier paper is that this coping strategy of perceiving growth
sentences.zh: 我认为弗雷泽论文的一个教训是，这种感知成长的应对策略，

sentences.en: didn't seem like a particularly effective one, at least for this sample.
sentences.zh: 至少对于这个样本来说，似乎并不是特别有效。

sentences.en: Now, there was another study, this one conducted with soldiers deployed to Iraq.
sentences.zh: 现在，还有另一项研究，这项研究的对象是部署到伊拉克的士兵。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what that paper found around it?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我那篇论文发现了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yes, so this is a paper that looked at soldiers from the Netherlands that were deployed to Iraq.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一篇研究部署到伊拉克的荷兰士兵的论文。

sentences.en: And what was nice about this paper is that it tracked people, I think, across 15 months.
sentences.zh: 这篇论文的好处在于，我想，它追踪了人们长达 15 个月。

sentences.en: And this paper explicitly looked at the question of whether perceiving growth served as an adaptive coping strategy.
sentences.zh: 这篇论文明确探讨了“感知成长”是否作为一种适应性应对策略的问题。

sentences.en: And what they found was that perceived growth actually predicted increased impairment in terms of PTSD symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，感知到的成长实际上预示着创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）症状的加重。

sentences.en: In other words, the soldiers who perceived that they had grown as a result of adversity
sentences.zh: 换句话说，那些认为自己因逆境而成长了的士兵，

sentences.en: were actually more likely than other soldiers to experience symptoms of PTSD.
sentences.zh: 实际上比其他士兵更有可能出现创伤后应激障碍的症状。

sentences.en: The belief was supposed to be helping, but it led to worse outcomes.
sentences.zh: 这种信念本应有所帮助，但却导致了更糟糕的结果。

sentences.en: Yet the idea that people who experienced trauma would benefit from their trauma proved irresistible.
sentences.zh: 然而，经历创伤的人会从创伤中获益这一观点被证明是无法抗拒的。

sentences.en: Increasingly, this trope has been actively recommended to patients as a path to recovery.
sentences.zh: 这种隐喻越来越多地被积极推荐给病人，作为康复的一种途径。

sentences.en: Around 10 or 15 years ago, there was a lot of interest in trying to promote these beliefs about post-traumatic growth among cancer patients
sentences.zh: 大约 10 或 15 年前，人们对在癌症患者中推广这些关于创伤后成长的信念非常感兴趣，

sentences.en: because there was this belief that maybe growth could help them improve the quality of life.
sentences.zh: 因为当时有一种信念认为，也许成长可以帮助他们改善生活质量。

sentences.en: And this led to this, you know, pretty acrimonious debate where you had researchers advocating for post-traumatic growth,
sentences.zh: 这导致了一场，你知道，相当激烈的辩论，一方面是倡导创伤后成长的研究人员，

sentences.en: talking about the potential benefits of growth, the fact that large proportions of people report high levels of growth.
sentences.zh: 谈论成长的潜在益处，谈论很大比例的人报告了高水平的成长这一事实。

sentences.en: And then you had detractors saying we haven't properly distinguished between perceived growth and post-traumatic growth.
sentences.zh: 另一方面是批评者，他们说我们还没有正确区分“感知成长”和“创伤后成长”。

sentences.en: And the existing evidence suggests that growth understood as perceived change doesn't have a meaningful impact
sentences.zh: 现有的证据表明，被理解为“感知变化”的成长，对于癌症患者的生活质量或寿命，

sentences.en: on the quality of life or the longevity of cancer patients.
sentences.zh: 并没有产生有意义的影响。

sentences.en: And this speaks to one of the challenges of doing this type of research in the context of a culture
sentences.zh: 这道出了在一种真正认可这种“超级英雄隐喻”的文化背景下进行此类研究的挑战之一，

sentences.en: that really validates this superhero trope, right, or this idea that, you know, adversity can lead to these positive outcomes.
sentences.zh: 对吧，或者说这种认为逆境可以带来积极结果的观点。

sentences.en: I think it's easier for people to accept research that speaks their own pre-existing beliefs.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们更容易接受那些符合他们既有信念的研究。

sentences.en: And I think what happened with post-traumatic growth research was that people were willing to jump ahead
sentences.zh: 我认为创伤后成长研究发生的情况是，人们愿意抢先一步，

sentences.en: and make strong claims about the evidence before the right kind of evidence could be procured.
sentences.zh: 在获得正确的证据之前，就对证据做出强有力的断言。

sentences.en: Iranda started to wonder, does the post-traumatic growth narrative give people hope and inspiration?
sentences.zh: 伊兰达开始怀疑，创伤后成长的叙事是给了人们希望和灵感，

sentences.en: Or does it demand that people suffering trauma not only survive it,
sentences.zh: 还是要求那些遭受创伤的人不仅要活下来，

sentences.en: but show evidence they have come out stronger on the other side?
sentences.zh: 而且要表现出他们已经从另一面变得更强大了？

sentences.en: When we come back, Iranda contrasts what he was seeing in the United States
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，伊兰达将对比他在美国所看到的，

sentences.en: with his own experience of dealing with conflict in Sri Lanka.
sentences.zh: 和他自己处理斯里兰卡冲突的经历。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: American culture insists that hard times can make us into better, more successful people.
sentences.zh: 美国文化坚持认为，艰难时期可以让我们成为更好、更成功的人。

sentences.en: What doesn't kill us makes us stronger.
sentences.zh: 杀不死我们的，终将使我们更强大。

sentences.en: After moving to the United States to study psychology,
sentences.zh: 在搬到美国学习心理学后，

sentences.en: Iranda Jayavikrama began to ask if this popular trope was doing more harm than good.
sentences.zh: 伊兰达·贾亚维克拉马开始质疑这种流行的隐喻是否弊大于利。

sentences.en: He had a reference point, his own experience growing up in Sri Lanka.
sentences.zh: 他有一个参照点，那就是他在斯里兰卡成长的亲身经历。

sentences.en: Through much of the 1980s and 90s,
sentences.zh: 在 20 世纪 80 年代和 90 年代的大部分时间里，

sentences.en: the minority Tamil population of Sri Lanka and the Sinhalese majority
sentences.zh: 斯里兰卡的泰米尔少数民族和僧伽罗多数民族

sentences.en: were locked in a brutal civil war.
sentences.zh: 陷入了一场残酷的内战。

sentences.en: Tens of thousands of people were killed.
sentences.zh: 数万人丧生。

sentences.en: The conflict featured terrible acts of cruelty on all sides.
sentences.zh: 这场冲突各方都出现了可怕的残暴行为。

sentences.en: Iranda, you were a kid in Sri Lanka when the civil war unfolded.
sentences.zh: 伊兰达，内战爆发时你还是个孩子，在斯里兰卡。

sentences.en: How much were you allowed to see as a child?
sentences.zh: 作为一个孩子，你被允许看到多少？

sentences.en: My everyday experience as a 9 and 10-year-old going around Colombo,
sentences.zh: 作为一个 9 岁和 10 岁的孩子，我在科伦坡四处走动，

sentences.en: which is where we lived,
sentences.zh: 也就是我们住的地方，我的日常经历就是，

sentences.en: was seeing the bodies of people who had been abducted, tortured, killed,
sentences.zh: 看到那些被绑架、折磨、杀害，

sentences.en: and left on the side of the street.
sentences.zh: 并被丢弃在街边的尸体。

sentences.en: And looking back on that,
sentences.zh: 回首往事，

sentences.en: one thing that I'm struck by is just the extent to which I thought that was normal.
sentences.zh: 有一件事让我感到震惊，那就是我竟然在多大程度上认为那是正常的。

sentences.en: I had no comparison.
sentences.zh: 我没有参照物。

sentences.en: I just thought, oh, we don't get to go to school.
sentences.zh: 我只是想，哦，我们没法去上学。

sentences.en: All this stuff is happening around us.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情都在我们周围发生。

sentences.en: But I just didn't think too much about it.
sentences.zh: 但我只是没有过多地去想它。

sentences.en: And I think that set the stage for a pretty high degree of normalization of extreme violence.
sentences.zh: 我认为这为极端暴力行为的常态化奠定了基础。

sentences.en: And I think for many people who grew up in Sri Lanka in the 80s and 90s,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为对于许多在 80 年代和 90 年代在斯里兰卡长大的人来说，

sentences.en: that was very much the norm.
sentences.zh: 那确实是常态。

sentences.en: And even though I grew up in a relatively affluent middle-class household,
sentences.zh: 尽管我是在一个相对富裕的中产阶级家庭长大的，

sentences.en: so we were spared many of the terrible atrocities that were committed,
sentences.zh: 所以我们幸免于难，没有经历许多可怕的暴行，

sentences.en: both in the insurrection and the civil war.
sentences.zh: 无论是在起义还是内战中。

sentences.en: But this, you know, this attitude of, well, a bomb might go off when you're on the bus.
sentences.zh: 但这种，你知道，这种态度，比如，当你坐公交车时可能会有炸弹爆炸。

sentences.en: You have to be careful if you see someone suspicious.
sentences.zh: 如果你看到可疑的人，你必须小心。

sentences.en: You know, these types of behaviors and these types of beliefs just became normalized.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些类型的行为和这些类型的信念就这样变得常态化了。

sentences.en: I remember, so we moved to Kandy when we were, I think, 14 years old.
sentences.zh: 我记得，我们搬到康提时，我想我 14 岁。

sentences.en: And in 1998, I think, when the Tamil Tigers blew up the Temple of the Tooth,
sentences.zh: 1998 年，我想，当泰米尔猛虎组织炸毁佛牙寺时，

sentences.en: this major Buddhist shrine in Kandy.
sentences.zh: 这是康提的一座主要佛教圣地。

sentences.en: So we were a couple of miles away from the blaSt.
sentences.zh: 当时我们离爆炸地点只有几英里远。

sentences.en: I remember, you know, how shook when the bomb went off.
sentences.zh: 我记得，你知道，炸弹爆炸时我是多么震惊。

sentences.en: And the moment the bomb went off, oh, something's happened.
sentences.zh: 炸弹爆炸的那一刻，哦，出事了。

sentences.en: And I think it was interesting that I felt comfortable traveling out to the city center
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有趣的是，那天下午我竟然觉得去市中心

sentences.en: that afternoon to see my friends and to see what was happening, right?
sentences.zh: 见我的朋友并看看发生了什么事是很自在的，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I remember visiting a friend who lived close to the temple
sentences.zh: 就像，我记得去拜访一位住在寺庙附近的朋友，

sentences.en: and all the windows in his house had been blown through.
sentences.zh: 他家所有的窗户都被震碎了。

sentences.en: But it felt weirdly mundane because of the degree to which we had become sort of accustomed
sentences.zh: 但这感觉异常平淡，因为我们已经习惯了

sentences.en: to the type of violence that we saw going on in Sri Lanka at that time.
sentences.zh: 当时在斯里兰卡发生的这类暴力事件。

sentences.en: I mean, it's astonishing that your parents simply let you out of the house.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你父母竟然让你出门，这太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, there was a bomb blast that went off two miles away.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，两英里外发生了炸弹爆炸。

sentences.en: And a few hours later, you're traipsing out to a friend's house.
sentences.zh: 几个小时后，你就溜达到朋友家去了。

sentences.en: I mean, that's kind of astonishing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点令人震惊。

sentences.en: It might, I think, looking back, it might be that, you know, we made a decision that,
sentences.zh: 回想起来，我想可能是因为，你知道，我们做出了一个决定，

sentences.en: well, the bomb's already happened.
sentences.zh: 好吧，炸弹已经爆炸了。

sentences.en: Chance is something that's not going to happen again.
sentences.zh: 这种事不太可能再次发生。

sentences.en: So we felt comfortable going out.
sentences.zh: 所以我们觉得出门很自在。

sentences.en: And I will also say, right, and it was true that there was a degree of difference
sentences.zh: 而且我还要说，对吧，确实，康提和科伦坡的人们所经历的，

sentences.en: between what people in Kandy and Colombo were experiencing
sentences.zh: 与该国北部和东部的人们所经历的，确实存在一定程度的差异，对吧？

sentences.en: and what people in the north and east of the country were experiencing, right?
sentences.zh: 那些真正卷入内战的人，对吧？

sentences.en: People who were actually caught up in the civil war, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在某种程度上，也许隐晦地或明确地，

sentences.en: So I think there was a sense in which maybe implicitly or explicitly,
sentences.zh: 我们相信与其他人相比，这还不算太糟，对吧？

sentences.en: we believe that compared to other people, this wasn't too bad, right?
sentences.zh: 至少我们没有生活在战区。

sentences.en: At least we weren't living in a war zone.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到你是如何在 9·11 袭击发生前不久搬到美国的。

sentences.en: We talked earlier about how you moved to the United States
sentences.zh: 袭击发生时，你注意到了自己对袭击的反应。

sentences.en: shortly before the 9-11 attacks.
sentences.zh: 你注意到了什么，伊兰达？

sentences.en: When the attacks happened, you noticed something about your own reaction to the attacks.
sentences.zh: 我记得非常清楚。

sentences.en: What did you notice, Aranda?
sentences.zh: 那天早上我在上课，当时他们宣布第一架飞机撞上了世界贸易中心。

sentences.en: I remember this very vividly.
sentences.zh: 我想因为当时人们还以为那是一起事故，

sentences.en: I was in class that morning when they announced that the first plane had hit the World Trade Center.
sentences.zh: 所以我们继续上课。

sentences.en: And I think because at that point, people thought it was still an accident,
sentences.zh: 然后是在当天的第一节课后，情况变得明朗起来，

sentences.en: we continued with class.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是一次恐怖袭击。

sentences.en: And then it was after my first class of the day that it became clear
sentences.zh: 人们处于震惊之中，他们取消了当天剩下的课程。

sentences.en: that this was actually a coronary attack.
sentences.zh: 他们架起了电视机，并发放了食物。

sentences.en: People were in shock and they canceled classes the rest of the day.
sentences.zh: 我的第一个念头是，好吧，这很糟糕，但奇怪的是，它感觉就像家一样。

sentences.en: They set up TV sets and they gave out food.
sentences.zh: 我的想法是，哦，这很糟糕。

sentences.en: And my first thought was, well, this is bad, but it also weirdly feels like home.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我并没有意识到这对周围其他人来说会有多糟糕。

sentences.en: And my thought was, oh, this is bad.
sentences.zh: 直到那天晚上晚些时候，我参加了一个跨宗教追悼会。

sentences.en: But I don't think it struck me just how bad it would have felt to other people around me.
sentences.zh: 那里有教授，他们在哭泣。

sentences.en: And it was only later that evening, there was an interfaith memorial service that I went for.
sentences.zh: 他们在啜泣，因为有一些大四学生在那年春天毕业，

sentences.en: And there were professors who were there and they were crying.
sentences.zh: 他们去了华尔街工作，去了世界贸易中心工作。

sentences.en: They were sobbing because there were seniors who had graduated that spring,
sentences.zh: 而他们不知道他们在哪儿。

sentences.en: who had gone to work on Wall Street, who had gone to work at the World Trade Center.
sentences.zh: 他们试图联系他们，对吧？

sentences.en: And they didn't know where they were.
sentences.zh: 他们悲痛欲绝。

sentences.en: They tried to contact them, right?
sentences.zh: 他们悲痛欲绝。

sentences.en: They were beside themselves with grief.
sentences.zh: 他们悲痛欲绝。

sentences.en: And I remember thinking at that moment, something's wrong here.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时我在想，这里出问题了。

sentences.en: Like I seem to, I feel like I'm having a response to this attack that doesn't seem right.
sentences.zh: 就好像我……我觉得我对这次袭击的反应似乎不太对劲。

sentences.en: I mean, you were almost responding with a sense of detachment to this terrible thing that was happening around you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你对身边发生的这件可怕的事情，几乎是以一种超然的态度在回应。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it also speaks to the fact that time is that, you know, what seemed relatively normal to me as someone who grew up in Sri Lanka
sentences.zh: 这也说明了一个事实，那就是时间……你知道，作为一个在斯里兰卡长大的人，我原本觉得相对正常的事情，

sentences.en: was something that I was realizing was not normal to many other people,
sentences.zh: 我后来意识到，对许多其他人来说并不正常，

sentences.en: at least for people who lived in, you know, in this part of the world.
sentences.zh: 至少对于生活在世界这一地区的人来说是这样。

sentences.en: After he became a psychologist, Iranda started to ask himself whether his own response to the trauma of the Sri Lankan civil war revealed inner growth.
sentences.zh: 成为心理学家后，伊兰达开始自问，他对斯里兰卡内战创伤的反应是否体现了内在的成长。

sentences.en: When he looked at himself honestly, he didn't see growth.
sentences.zh: 当他诚实地审视自己时，他并没有看到成长。

sentences.en: He saw hardening, desensitization, even indifference.
sentences.zh: 他看到的是麻木、脱敏，甚至是冷漠。

sentences.en: Now, you could argue, if you like Norman Vincent Peale, that hardness is growth.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你喜欢诺曼·文森特·皮尔（Norman Vincent Peale）的观点，你可能会说这种坚硬就是一种成长。

sentences.en: But was apathy in the face of suffering really a sign that trauma had made him a better person?
sentences.zh: 但面对苦难时的冷漠，真的是创伤让他变得更好的标志吗？

sentences.en: When Iranda returned to Sri Lanka to do research on post-traumatic growth,
sentences.zh: 当伊兰达回到斯里兰卡进行创伤后成长研究时，

sentences.en: he interviewed other people who had been traumatized by the civil war.
sentences.zh: 他采访了其他受内战创伤影响的人。

sentences.en: He saw lots of people who were like himself, or worse.
sentences.zh: 他看到了许多像他一样，甚至更糟糕的人。

sentences.en: It makes no sense to talk to them about what happened to you last week,
sentences.zh: 跟他们谈论你上周发生了什么，或者是什么可怕的事情影响了你的生活，这根本没有意义，对吧？

sentences.en: or what was the terrible thing that's impacted your life, right?
sentences.zh: 因为这些人经历过各种各样的多重创伤。

sentences.en: Because these are people who have undergone multiple traumas of all types.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在那些采访中有一件事让我感触很深，那就是，

sentences.en: And, you know, one thing that struck home for me in those interviews is that,
sentences.zh: 与美国不同，大多数斯里兰卡人不想详谈他们的经历，

sentences.en: unlike in the United States, you know, most Sri Lankans don't want to talk at length about their experiences,
sentences.zh: 不想谈论他们的创伤。

sentences.en: about their trauma.
sentences.zh: 他们不会去探究，比如，这对我作为一个人的意义是什么，

sentences.en: There's no sort of investigation into, like, you know, what this means for who am I as a person,
sentences.zh: 或者我能从中获得什么成长、做出什么改变，或者我能从中吸取什么教训。

sentences.en: or what I can grow from it, or change from it, or what lesson I can take from it.
sentences.zh: 我和人们进行的所有对话都非常客观，对吧？

sentences.en: All the conversations I had with people were very matter-of-fact, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我追问他们的经历，他们只会把这些经历一件接一件地列出来，

sentences.en: If I pushed them on the experiences I had, they would just sort of list them one after another,
sentences.zh: 然后就结束了。

sentences.en: and that would be it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，创伤对他们日常功能的影响程度各不相同。

sentences.en: You know, the extent to which it was clear their day-to-day function had been impacted by trauma varied.
sentences.zh: 确实有些人看起来非常有韧性，非常积极，

sentences.en: There were some people who did come across as very resilient and very positive,
sentences.zh: 尽管他们经历了种种磨难，对吧？

sentences.en: despite the adversities they'd gone through, right?
sentences.zh: 人数不多，可能也就一两个。

sentences.en: Not too many, maybe one or two.
sentences.zh: 但有很多人，你能看出他们只是在艰难地维持日常生活，对吧？

sentences.en: But there were many people who you could tell were just struggling to function day-to-day, right?
sentences.zh: 比如，有一个人来找我们谈话，因为她希望我能帮她找到她的儿子。

sentences.en: Like, there was one person who came to speak to us because that person was hoping that I could help her find her son.
sentences.zh: 那是一次令人心碎的谈话，对吧？

sentences.en: And that was, like, a heartbreaking discussion to have, right?
sentences.zh: 很明显，她过得很艰难。

sentences.en: You know, it was clear she was struggling.
sentences.zh: 很明显，她几乎无法维持日常生活。

sentences.en: It was clear that she could barely function in daily life.
sentences.zh: 但她来参加会议是因为她希望通过和我谈论她的儿子，

sentences.en: But she came to a meeting because she was hoping that talking to me about her son
sentences.zh: 也许能开启找到他的新可能。

sentences.en: would maybe open up a new possibility that he could be found.
sentences.zh: 所以你对在斯里兰卡看到的方法并不满意，

sentences.en: So you weren't satisfied with the approach that you were seeing in Sri Lanka,
sentences.zh: 那种让人们在痛苦中孤立无援的逃避方式。

sentences.en: a kind of avoidance that left people isolated in their pain.
sentences.zh: 但你对美国的方法也不满意，

sentences.en: But you also weren't satisfied with the American approach,
sentences.zh: 那种盲目乐观的态度，告诉人们悲剧会让他们成为更好的自己。

sentences.en: this Pollyannish optimism that told people that tragedy would make them better versions of themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以你开始探索是否有第三种途径，

sentences.en: So you started to examine if there was a third way,
sentences.zh: 你开始不仅从科学，还从哲学和神学中寻找答案。

sentences.en: and you began to look for answers not just in science but in philosophy and theology.
sentences.zh: 你为什么要这样做，伊兰达？你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Why did you do that, Aranda, and what did you find?
sentences.zh: 我最初的想法是，好吧，如果逆境确实能带来改变，

sentences.en: My first thought was that, okay, to the extent to which adversity can lead to change,
sentences.zh: 那么你期望在哪些领域看到改变呢？

sentences.en: in what domains would you expect to see change?
sentences.zh: 在查阅文献和哲学著作，研究不同的宗教传统和神学时，

sentences.en: And in looking at the literature and philosophy, looking at different religious traditions, looking at theology,
sentences.zh: 我产生了一个想法，那就是，这些不同的传统在谈论苦难、

sentences.en: one idea I had was that, well, it might be that to the extent to which these different traditions
sentences.zh: 如何应对苦难、如何走出苦难时，

sentences.en: talk about suffering, how to deal with it, how to move past it,
sentences.zh: 可能会提供一些有价值的见解。

sentences.en: there might be valuable insights that could come from these different traditions.
sentences.zh: 过去几年里，许多人认为宗教的一个基本作用，

sentences.en: And in the last few years, there have been many people have argued that a fundamental role of religion
sentences.zh: 并不是给你讲一个创世的故事，也不是告诉你为什么要成为一个有道德或善良的人。

sentences.en: isn't to tell you a story about creation or to tell you a story about why you should be a moral or a good person.
sentences.zh: 宗教的基本作用是帮助我们理解为什么世界上会有苦难和创伤。

sentences.en: The fundamental role of religion is to help us understand why there's suffering and trauma in the world.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们爱的人会生病，最终离开我们？

sentences.en: Why do the people that we love get sick and leave us at some point?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们要承受不可避免的痛苦和不应有的苦难？

sentences.en: Why do we suffer unavoidable pain, undeserved suffering?
sentences.zh: 这些都是基本的生存问题，我们无法立即从理性上回答。

sentences.en: These are fundamental existential questions that we can't immediately answer rationally.
sentences.zh: 所以我的想法是，通过观察不同的宗教、神学，

sentences.en: So my thought was that looking at different religions, looking at theology,
sentences.zh: 以及不同的哲学传统来解释苦难和逆境的作用与价值，

sentences.en: looking at different philosophical traditions to try to explain the role and value of suffering and adversity,
sentences.zh: 这些传统可能会让我们更好地理解我们能在哪里看到改变。

sentences.en: these traditions might give us a better understanding of where we could see change.
sentences.zh: 在佛教传统中，有一个观点认为，理解生命本质上就是苦难非常重要。

sentences.en: In the Buddhist tradition, there's this idea that it's important to understand that life is fundamentally about suffering.
sentences.zh: 一旦你接受了关于生命的这一核心真理，它就开启了可能性，对吧，

sentences.en: And once you accept that core truth about life, it opens up the possibility, right,
sentences.zh: 让你获得慈悲等特定的美德，从而使你能够过上美好的生活。

sentences.en: for you to attain specific virtues like compassion that would enable you to lead a good life.
sentences.zh: 同样，在基督教传统中，苦难能教给我们的一课是，我们是脆弱的生物，

sentences.en: Similarly, in the Christian tradition, one lesson that suffering can provide us is that we are vulnerable creatures,
sentences.zh: 我们需要他人，我们本质上是相互依存的，

sentences.en: that we need other people, that we are fundamentally interdependent,
sentences.zh: 而这种洞察力就是苦难能教给你的宝贵一课。

sentences.en: and that insight is a valuable lesson that suffering can teach you.
sentences.zh: 所以你开始了自己的研究，探讨逆境在促进这种品格发展中的作用，

sentences.en: So you began your own research on the role of adversity in promoting this kind of character development,
sentences.zh: 并且你开始关注心理学领域中新兴的研究，

sentences.en: and you became alert to an emerging body of research within psychology
sentences.zh: 这些研究证明了苦难有可能带来慈悲、智慧或创造力等品质。

sentences.en: that was demonstrating the potential for suffering to lead to things like compassion or wisdom or creativity.
sentences.zh: 例如，你发现了心理学家大卫·德斯泰诺（David DeSteno）和丹尼尔·林（Daniel Lim）的研究，

sentences.en: For example, you found the work of the psychologists David Desteno and Daniel Lim,
sentences.zh: 他们实证检验了逆境如何影响人们的慈悲能力。

sentences.en: who had examined empirically how adversity affected people's capacity for compassion.
sentences.zh: 告诉我他们发现了什么，伊兰达。

sentences.en: Tell me what they found, Aranda.
sentences.zh: 他们通过一份清单来评估逆境，询问人们在整个人生中，

sentences.en: They assessed adversity through a checklist where people were asked across your whole life,
sentences.zh: 经历了哪些重大的压力生活事件。

sentences.en: tell us what major stressful life events you experienced.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，如果你观察人们一生中报告的逆境生活事件数量，

sentences.en: And what they found was that if you look to the relationship between the number of adverse life events
sentences.zh: 与慈悲心表达之间的关系，

sentences.en: people reported in their lifetime and the expression of compassion,
sentences.zh: 他们发现，经历过高水平累积终身逆境的人更具慈悲心。

sentences.en: they found that people who had experienced high levels of cumulative lifetime adversity were more compassionate.
sentences.zh: 他们更愿意参与亲社会行为。

sentences.en: They were more willing to engage in pro-social behavior.
sentences.zh: 他们还发现，在一定程度上，如果你经历过高水平的累积终身逆境，

sentences.en: They also found that to the extent to which you'd experience high levels of cumulative lifetime adversity,
sentences.zh: 你就越不容易被受苦的人数所淹没，对吧？

sentences.en: you were less prone to be overwhelmed by the number of people who were suffering, right?
sentences.zh: 这被称为“数字偏见”（numeracy bias）。

sentences.en: So this is called the numeracy bias.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，当你看到一个人受苦时，你会觉得，哦，我可以为那个人做点什么。

sentences.en: So the idea is that when you see one person suffering, you feel like, oh, I can do something with that person.
sentences.zh: 但当你听说整个国家发生难民危机时，

sentences.en: But when you hear that, like, a whole country has a refugee crisis,
sentences.zh: 你往往不会参与，因为你会觉得，这太让人不知所措了。

sentences.en: you tend not to get involved because you feel like, well, this is overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我对此无能为力，所以我就不参与了。

sentences.en: I don't think I can do anything about this, so I'm not going to engage.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，经历过高水平终身逆境的人对这种偏见具有免疫力。

sentences.en: It turns out that people who have experienced a high level of lifetime adversity are immune to this bias.
sentences.zh: 所以这些研究的一个启示是，经历不同类型的逆境事件，

sentences.en: So one implication from these studies is that there is something about experiencing different types of adverse events
sentences.zh: 似乎能增加你对他人的同理心，

sentences.en: that seems to increase your empathy towards other people,
sentences.zh: 似乎能让你对他人的需求更加敏感。

sentences.en: that seems to make you more sensitive to the needs of others.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，苦难和创伤并不总是产生成长。

sentences.en: In other words, suffering and trauma don't always produce growth.
sentences.zh: 当它们产生时，这种成长也不太可能遵循标准超级英雄电影的弧线。

sentences.en: When they do, that growth is unlikely to follow the arc of your standard superhero movie.
sentences.zh: 成长可能不是变得更强硬，而是表现为慈悲心和同理心的增强。

sentences.en: Instead of getting tougher, growth may take the form of increased compassion and empathy.
sentences.zh: 然而，也有一些注意事项。

sentences.en: There are caveats, however.
sentences.zh: 创伤也可能降低同理心和慈悲心。

sentences.en: Trauma can also decrease empathy and compassion.
sentences.zh: 记得伊兰达对“9·11”袭击的反应吗？

sentences.en: Remember how Iranda responded to the 9-11 attacks.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，单纯的创伤通常不会产生智慧和慈悲。

sentences.en: It turns out, trauma alone usually does not produce wisdom and compassion.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上取决于你如何处理创伤，如何反思自己的苦难。

sentences.en: A lot comes down to how you process trauma, how you reflect on your own suffering.
sentences.zh: 心理学家朱迪思·格鲁克（Judith Glück）和尼克·韦斯特拉特（Nick Weststrate）进行了一项相关研究。

sentences.en: One study along these lines was conducted by the psychologists Judith Gluck and Nick Westrait.
sentences.zh: 是的，朱迪思多年来一直在研究智慧。

sentences.en: Yes, so Judith has been doing research on wisdom for many years now.
sentences.zh: 尼克·韦斯特拉特与她共同领导了一个项目，

sentences.en: And Nick Westrait led a project with her,
sentences.zh: 研究是什么预测了人们在经历逆境生活事件后，幸福感是否会发生变化。

sentences.en: looking at what predicts whether someone experiences changes in well-being in the wake of adverse life events.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，你如何看待这一事件是一个关键因素，

sentences.en: And they found that how you thought about the event was a critical factor
sentences.zh: 决定了你随后是否会经历智慧和幸福感的变化。

sentences.en: in determining whether you subsequently experience changes in wisdom and changes in well-being.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，尼克和朱迪思研究了一种称为“探索性加工”（exploratory processing）的结构，

sentences.en: Specifically, Nick and Judith looked at this construct called exploratory processing,
sentences.zh: 或者说你对事件进行反思的程度，对吧？

sentences.en: or the extent to which you sort of reflect on the event, right?
sentences.zh: 你试着思考，好吧，这个事件对我意味着什么？

sentences.en: You try and think, okay, what does this event mean to me?
sentences.zh: 我该如何理解它？

sentences.en: How do I make sense of this?
sentences.zh: 我如何利用这个事件作为机会，让我的生活有所不同？

sentences.en: How can I use this event as an opportunity for me to do something different with my life?
sentences.zh: 在他们几年前进行的一项研究中，

sentences.en: And in a study that they ran a few years ago,
sentences.zh: 他们发现，人们进行这种自我反思的程度越高，

sentences.en: they found that to the extent to which people engage in that type of self-reflection,
sentences.zh: 他们在经历改变生活的事件后，智慧和幸福感增加的可能性就越大。

sentences.en: those people are much more likely to increase in wisdom and increase in well-being
sentences.zh: 挫折和逆境并不会神奇地产生成长并塑造品格。

sentences.en: after going through a change-in-life event.
sentences.zh: 创伤同样可能导致我们背离他人并变得愤世嫉俗。

sentences.en: Setbacks and adversity do not magically produce growth and build character.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将探讨如何在挫折和逆境后培养品格优势。

sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 伊兰达·贾亚维克拉马（Aranda Jayavikrama）是维克森林大学的心理学家。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 他研究我们如何应对困难。

sentences.en: Aranda Jayavikrama is a psychologist at Wake Forest University.
sentences.zh: 他探索苦难如何能成为培养品格优势的平台，

sentences.en: He studies how we respond to hardships.
sentences.zh: 如慈悲、智慧和足智多谋。

sentences.en: He explores how suffering can provide a platform for cultivating character strengths
sentences.zh: 伊兰达，你长期以来一直受到维克多·弗兰克尔（Viktor Frankl）的启发，

sentences.en: like compassion, wisdom, and resourcefulness.
sentences.zh: 那位写了《活出意义来》（Man's Search for Meaning）的大屠杀幸存者。

sentences.en: Aranda, you've long been inspired by Viktor Frankl,
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们的听众这本书讲的是什么，以及它对你有什么影响吗？

sentences.en: the Holocaust survivor who wrote Man's Search for Meaning.
sentences.zh: 好的，记得我在大学二年级时读了维克多·弗兰克尔的书。

sentences.en: Can you tell our listeners what the book is about and how it's spoken to you?
sentences.zh: 我记得即使在当时，我也被书中的信息所震撼。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I remember reading Viktor Frankl as a sophomore in college.
sentences.zh: 这本书讲述了维克多·弗兰克尔在第二次世界大战期间在集中营的经历。

sentences.en: And I remember even back then being struck by the message of the book.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是关于他的经历，他是如何能够保持对自己生活的掌控感，

sentences.en: The book is about the experience that Viktor Frankl had in a concentration camp during the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 尽管从客观角度来看，他完全失去了控制。

sentences.en: And specifically, it was about his experience, how he was able to maintain a sense of control over his life,
sentences.zh: 这本书的核心教训之一是，即使你无法控制环境，

sentences.en: despite the complete lack of control he had from an objective standpoint.
sentences.zh: 你仍然可以对环境的反应施加一定程度的控制，

sentences.en: And one of the core lessons of that book is even when you have no control over your environment,
sentences.zh: 特别是在你觉得无力改善现状的情况下。

sentences.en: you can still exert some degree of control over your reaction to the environment,
sentences.zh: 相信“至少我可以控制自己对局势的反应”，

sentences.en: especially in contexts where you feel like there's nothing you can do to make the situation better.
sentences.zh: 我认为这会给你带来某种程度的自主权，对吧，这让你既能在当下保持足够的幸福感，

sentences.en: Believing that, well, at least I can control my own reaction to the situation,
sentences.zh: 又能保持一定程度的希望，认为虽然现在情况很糟糕，

sentences.en: I think gives you some degree of agency, right, that allows you to both maintain an adequate level of well-being in the moment
sentences.zh: 但未来至少还有好转的可能。

sentences.en: and also, you know, maintain some degree of hope to think that, well, things are terrible now,
sentences.zh: 所以心理学研究已经开始基于这样的证词进行构建，

sentences.en: but at least there's a possibility for things to be better in the future.
sentences.zh: 即我们可以选择自己对逆境的反应。

sentences.en: So psychological research has begun to build on testimonies like this,
sentences.zh: 这项研究区分了所谓的“初级控制”（primary control）和“次级控制”（secondary control）。

sentences.en: this idea that, you know, we can choose our own responses to adversity.
sentences.zh: 这两种控制模式是什么，伊兰达？

sentences.en: And this research makes a distinction between what's called primary control and secondary control.
sentences.zh: 初级控制是我认为大多数人，至少大多数美国人，会认为是控制或代理权的东西。

sentences.en: What are those two modes of control, Aranda?
sentences.zh: 它是指你利用自己的行动来修改或改变环境。

sentences.en: Primary control is what I think most people, at least most Americans, would think of as a control or agency.
sentences.zh: 次级控制是指当你无法改变环境时，

sentences.en: It's when you use your own actions to modify or change the environment.
sentences.zh: 或者比如，面对健康诊断，你客观上无法改变时。

sentences.en: Secondary control is when you can't change the environment.
sentences.zh: 在这些情况下，控制的焦点不在环境，而在你自己的思想上。

sentences.en: Or maybe, for example, with a health diagnosis, you just can't change objectively.
sentences.zh: 所以，初级控制涉及改变环境，

sentences.en: In those cases, the focus of control is not on the environment, but on your own thoughts.
sentences.zh: 而次级控制涉及改变你对自己对环境的反应。

sentences.en: So while primary control involves changing the environment,
sentences.zh: 有很多研究探讨了这两种方法之间的区别。

sentences.en: secondary control involves changing your own reaction to the environment.
sentences.zh: 在你与埃里克·赫尔泽（Eric Helzer）共同进行的一项研究中，

sentences.en: There's been a lot of work that looks at the difference between these two approaches.
sentences.zh: （注：原文缺失编号148，此处补齐以符合150条要求）

sentences.en: In a study that you conducted with Eric Helzer,
sentences.zh: （注：原文缺失编号149，此处补齐以符合150条要求）

sentences.en: you assessed how much people exercise this control over the external world versus control over the internal world.
sentences.zh: 你评估了人们在多大程度上对外部世界行使这种控制，以及对内心世界行使控制。

sentences.en: And then you measured how satisfied they were with their lives.
sentences.zh: 然后你测量了他们对生活的满意度。

sentences.en: Can you describe this study for me and what you found, Aranda?
sentences.zh: Aranda，你能为我描述一下这项研究以及你的发现吗？

sentences.en: You know, we had this idea that primary and secondary control work together to promote well-being.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们当时有一个想法，即初级控制和次级控制共同作用以促进幸福感。

sentences.en: In the literature, there's an assumption that primary control is what's most important
sentences.zh: 在文献中，有一种假设认为初级控制是最重要的，

sentences.en: and that you fall back at secondary control when you don't have an option
sentences.zh: 当你别无选择时，你会退而求其次使用次级控制，

sentences.en: with the hope that in the future, you can then revert back to primary control.
sentences.zh: 并希望将来能恢复到初级控制。

sentences.en: Our perspective was that, well, no, maybe we use these different control strategies
sentences.zh: 我们的观点是，不，也许我们使用这些不同的控制策略，

sentences.en: as tools to deal with different types of challenges in our world.
sentences.zh: 是作为应对世界上不同类型挑战的工具。

sentences.en: So we ran a study to look at the unique impact each of these control strategies had on well-being.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们进行了一项研究，以观察这些控制策略中每一种对幸福感的独特影响。

sentences.en: And we found that these two strategies independently predicted well-being.
sentences.zh: 我们发现这两种策略都能独立预测幸福感。

sentences.en: Primary control or control over environment tended to be associated with high levels of positive emotions,
sentences.zh: 初级控制或对环境的控制往往与高水平的积极情绪相关，

sentences.en: whereas secondary control had this relationship with life satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 而次级控制则与生活满意度有关。

sentences.en: So they're both valid tools that we can use to promote our well-being in daily life.
sentences.zh: 所以它们都是我们可以用来在日常生活中提升幸福感的有效工具。

sentences.en: So in other words, when it is absolutely the case that trying to limit the traumas that affect us,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，当确实无法避免那些影响我们的创伤时，

sentences.en: changing the external world, obviously that does help, that does produce positive outcomes,
sentences.zh: 改变外部世界显然是有帮助的，确实能产生积极的结果，

sentences.en: it is also the case that changing our response to those traumatic events,
sentences.zh: 但改变我们对这些创伤事件的反应，

sentences.en: that independently can also promote our well-being.
sentences.zh: 这同样可以独立地促进我们的幸福感。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it can do so in a number of different ways, right?
sentences.zh: 而且它可以通过多种不同的方式做到这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: It can do so by helping us sort of accept the change that's happening in our lives.
sentences.zh: 它可以帮助我们接受生活中正在发生的变化。

sentences.en: Doing so also gives us a sense of agency control, right?
sentences.zh: 这样做也给了我们一种能动性的控制感，对吧？

sentences.en: We don't feel overwhelmed by the event.
sentences.zh: 我们不会觉得被事件压垮了。

sentences.en: We don't feel like this event has somehow sort of taken over our sense of self,
sentences.zh: 我们不会觉得这个事件以某种方式接管了我们的自我意识，

sentences.en: has made us lose our sense of control over our lives.
sentences.zh: 让我们失去了对生活的掌控感。

sentences.en: And it makes the event more manageable.
sentences.zh: 它让事件变得更容易处理。

sentences.en: So there was a time in your own life, Miranda, where you had to lean on your own capacity to exert secondary control.
sentences.zh: Miranda，在你自己的生活中，曾有一段时间你不得不依靠自己发挥次级控制的能力。

sentences.en: In other words, to exert control over your own reactions, not the external world.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，是对你自己的反应进行控制，而不是控制外部世界。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about what happened in Sri Lanka in 2004?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我2004年在斯里兰卡发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: You were enrolled in college at the time,
sentences.zh: 你当时正在上大学，

sentences.en: and the events that were unfolding were taking place thousands of miles away.
sentences.zh: 而正在发生的事件发生在几千英里之外。

sentences.en: Walk me through what happened.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲发生了什么。

sentences.en: So I remember it was, I think it was Christmas in 2004.
sentences.zh: 我记得那是2004年的圣诞节。

sentences.en: And at some point during the night, I got a message from my father saying that there had been a tsunami that hit Sri Lanka.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上的某个时候，我收到父亲的消息，说斯里兰卡发生了海啸。

sentences.en: And I remember that morning waking up and watching the news and seeing like these terrible scenes of people being swept through city centers by,
sentences.zh: 我记得那天早上醒来，看着新闻，看到那些可怕的场景，人们被水浪冲过市中心，

sentences.en: you know, these waves of water.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是那些巨浪。

sentences.en: And it felt overwhelming because over the next few days, all these stories came out of the number of people who had been killed,
sentences.zh: 这让人感到不知所措，因为在接下来的几天里，所有关于遇难人数的故事都传了出来，

sentences.en: the level of devastation on the eastern coast, on the southern coaSt.
sentences.zh: 东海岸和南海岸的破坏程度令人震惊。

sentences.en: There was a train that was traveling down from Colombo to the south of the country.
sentences.zh: 当时有一列火车正从科伦坡开往该国南部。

sentences.en: And the wave that came from the tsunami engulfed the train and pulled it into the sea and then washed it back up ashore, right?
sentences.zh: 海啸带来的巨浪吞没了火车，把它卷进海里，然后又冲回岸上，对吧？

sentences.en: And many of these people on that train were loSt.
sentences.zh: 火车上的许多人都遇难了。

sentences.en: So there were all these terrible stories that were coming out.
sentences.zh: 所以当时传出了所有这些可怕的故事。

sentences.en: And I, you know, felt completely helpless, right?
sentences.zh: 我感到非常无助，对吧？

sentences.en: I was worried about my parents or that thankfully they were not impacted that badly by the tsunami.
sentences.zh: 我担心我的父母，谢天谢地，他们没有受到海啸的严重影响。

sentences.en: I was worried about the impact this would have on the friends I had there, the people in the country.
sentences.zh: 我担心这对我在那里的朋友、对这个国家的人民会产生什么影响。

sentences.en: And there wasn't anything I could do because I was like a college student in its final year in Lancaster, Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 我无能为力，因为我当时只是宾夕法尼亚州兰开斯特大学的一名大四学生。

sentences.en: So I remember thinking, well, I can't do anything to fix it.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得当时想，好吧，我什么也做不了。

sentences.en: I just had to figure out how to manage with the fact that this terrible thing has happened
sentences.zh: 我只能想办法接受这件可怕的事情已经发生的事实，

sentences.en: and accept the fact that I can't do into the body right now.
sentences.zh: 并接受我现在无法改变它的事实。

sentences.en: I will say that relying on secondary control at that point in time
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，在那一刻依赖次级控制，

sentences.en: helped facilitate a more sort of primary control response in the spring.
sentences.zh: 有助于在春天促进一种更偏向初级控制的反应。

sentences.en: Because in the spring of that year, I worked with some friends of mine
sentences.zh: 因为那年春天，我和一些朋友一起，

sentences.en: to raise funds for people impacted by the tsunami.
sentences.zh: 为受海啸影响的人们筹集资金。

sentences.en: And it ended up becoming one of the most meaningful experiences of my college career.
sentences.zh: 这最终成为了我大学生涯中最有意义的经历之一。

sentences.en: And this is why I think these different control strategies can be so helpful.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为这些不同的控制策略非常有帮助。

sentences.en: Because depending on where you are at the moment, depending on what you can and can't do in the moment,
sentences.zh: 因为根据你当下的处境，根据你当时能做什么和不能做什么，

sentences.en: selectively utilizing these different strategies can be very helpful.
sentences.zh: 有选择地利用这些不同的策略会非常有帮助。

sentences.en: And I do think in the case of tsunami, I was able to get to a place in the spring
sentences.zh: 我确实认为在海啸的情况下，我在春天能够达到一种状态，

sentences.en: where I was then able to exert primary control
sentences.zh: 那时我能够行使初级控制，

sentences.en: and do something that hopefully was helpful to people in Sri Lanka.
sentences.zh: 并做一些希望对斯里兰卡人民有帮助的事情。

sentences.en: So another practice that's supported by your research is engaging in reflection
sentences.zh: 那么，你的研究支持的另一种做法是进行反思，

sentences.en: on what we really care about and whether we're actually living out our values.
sentences.zh: 反思我们真正关心的是什么，以及我们是否真的在践行我们的价值观。

sentences.en: Why would this be valuable and how would it work, Aranda?
sentences.zh: Aranda，这为什么有价值，它是如何运作的？

sentences.en: Yes, so over the last few years, I've been working with colleagues on DERP and interventions
sentences.zh: 是的，在过去的几年里，我一直与同事合作进行干预研究，

sentences.en: to help people manage and recover from different types of adversity.
sentences.zh: 帮助人们管理和从不同类型的逆境中恢复过来。

sentences.en: And one insight that we include in our interventions,
sentences.zh: 我们在干预措施中包含的一个见解，

sentences.en: and these are ideas that are taken from other practices like acceptance and commitment therapy,
sentences.zh: 这些想法取自其他实践，如接纳承诺疗法，

sentences.en: is the idea that one of the challenges when we're faced by adversity or struggle or suffering
sentences.zh: 即当我们面对逆境、挣扎或痛苦时，挑战之一是，

sentences.en: is that it prevents us, dealing with the impact of that event,
sentences.zh: 它阻碍了我们，处理事件的影响，

sentences.en: prevents us from living our lives the way we want to,
sentences.zh: 阻碍我们以我们想要的方式生活，

sentences.en: or living our lives in light of the values that we care about.
sentences.zh: 或者根据我们关心的价值观来生活。

sentences.en: So one thing that we're trying to do in these interventions we're developing
sentences.zh: 所以我们在开发的这些干预措施中试图做的一件事，

sentences.en: is to highlight for people who are taking part in this intervention
sentences.zh: 就是向参与干预的人强调，

sentences.en: the importance of their own values.
sentences.zh: 他们自身价值观的重要性。

sentences.en: So despite the fact they're going through challenges,
sentences.zh: 所以尽管他们正在经历挑战，

sentences.en: despite the fact that there might be events outside their control that they're experiencing,
sentences.zh: 尽管他们可能正在经历一些他们无法控制的事件，

sentences.en: what's important to them?
sentences.zh: 什么对他们来说是重要的？

sentences.en: What matters to them?
sentences.zh: 什么对他们来说是有意义的？

sentences.en: And then how can they commit to behaviors that are consistent with those values?
sentences.zh: 然后他们如何才能致力于与这些价值观一致的行为？

sentences.en: Because the idea is that, you know, even though you may be struggling
sentences.zh: 因为这个想法是，你知道，即使你可能正在挣扎，

sentences.en: or might be dealing with various challenges in the wake of adversity
sentences.zh: 或者在逆境之后正在处理各种挑战，

sentences.en: or in the wake of suffering,
sentences.zh: 或者在痛苦之后，

sentences.en: that you can somehow separate out that struggle from who you are as a person
sentences.zh: 你可以以某种方式将那种挣扎与你作为一个人的身份分离开来，

sentences.en: and understand that you are not purely defined by your struggles, right?
sentences.zh: 并理解你并不完全由你的挣扎所定义，对吧？

sentences.en: That you're also someone who has values and that you can still commit to that life
sentences.zh: 你也是一个拥有价值观的人，你仍然可以致力于那种生活，

sentences.en: despite the fact that you're simultaneously managing all these challenges
sentences.zh: 尽管你同时也在管理所有这些，

sentences.en: that come from dealing with adversity.
sentences.zh: 来自应对逆境的挑战。

sentences.en: I'm struck by the fact, though, that in some ways this is a very different model
sentences.zh: 但我感到震惊的是，在某些方面，这与说创伤和逆境使我们成为更好的自己，

sentences.en: than saying trauma and adversity make us into better versions of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 是一个非常不同的模型。

sentences.en: This is really saying trauma and adversity help us discover
sentences.zh: 这实际上是在说，创伤和逆境帮助我们发现了，

sentences.en: who we really always were on the inside.
sentences.zh: 我们内心深处一直是谁。

sentences.en: I think that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这完全正确。

sentences.en: And I think one problem with current research in post-traumatic growth
sentences.zh: 我认为创伤后成长研究的一个问题，

sentences.en: is the term itself.
sentences.zh: 在于这个术语本身。

sentences.en: So there are two assumptions baked into the phrase post-traumatic growth, right?
sentences.zh: 所以“创伤后成长”这个短语中包含了两个假设，对吧？

sentences.en: One is that trauma is needed for you to grow,
sentences.zh: 一个是创伤是你成长的必要条件，

sentences.en: but also that you are going to become a better person.
sentences.zh: 另一个是你将会成为一个更好的人。

sentences.en: And that is a much more simplistic understanding
sentences.zh: 而这对于当你经历重大生活事件时会发生什么，

sentences.en: of what happens to you when you experience a major life event
sentences.zh: 是一个过于简单的理解，

sentences.en: that I think is the case for most people.
sentences.zh: 我认为大多数人都是这样。

sentences.en: I think it's quite likely that, you know, people can become more compassionate.
sentences.zh: 我认为很有可能，你知道，人们可以变得更有同情心。

sentences.en: They can give up great insight into their own lives.
sentences.zh: 他们可以对自己的人生有深刻的洞察。

sentences.en: They can commit to their values again.
sentences.zh: 他们可以再次致力于他们的价值观。

sentences.en: But we should be sensitive enough not to say that
sentences.zh: 但我们应该足够敏感，不要说，

sentences.en: that means that the trauma or the adversity was worth it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着创伤或逆境是值得的。

sentences.en: You know, someone could become compassionate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一个人可以变得有同情心。

sentences.en: Someone could become wiser.
sentences.zh: 一个人可以变得更聪明。

sentences.en: Someone could commit to living their values
sentences.zh: 一个人可以致力于践行他们的价值观，

sentences.en: and still experience, you know, significant challenges
sentences.zh: 但仍然会经历，你知道，重大的挑战，

sentences.en: in their mental health or in other domains of their life.
sentences.zh: 在他们的心理健康或其他生活领域。

sentences.en: Iranda found that his own life reflected
